newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen rebounding.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen rebounding.

text.p: Polish shares eased on Monday, falling for the second straight session, but analysts said the stronger buying after price fixing signalled the market's mood was good and that slow growth should start on Tuesday.

Analysts said one reason for the generally good climate was anticipation of a repeat of this year's January rise, possibly fuelled by institutional buying that has held back in December so as not to threaten 1996's gains.
"At the start of the year many large institutions that didn't want to open a position at the end of the year might buy," said Jan Koch, a traderat Polish Development Bank (PBR).

The main market's all-share WIG index eased 0.2 percent to 14,143.8 points and turnover rose 5.4 percent to 75.8 million zlotys ($26.4 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 37 to 25 with 21 stocks flat.
Analysts said the main index could approach 14,500 points some time next month.

They said a good sign was that the market was not dropping despite the central bank's statements that interest rates could rise as early as the second half of January to curb fast credit growth, though some said the news was already priced in.

Analysts said paintmaker Polifarb Wroclaw and furniture maker Swarzedz fell 5.7 and four percent in profit-taking after surges, the former after it said it would merge with Polifarb Cieszyn, the latter after a 200-million-mark deal.
They blamed low turnovers for the extent of the 9.5 and 8.7 percent falls by insurer Polisa and construction firm Mostostal Zabrze, though Zabrze's fall came after recent gains.

Continuous trade turnover was at 3.1 million zlotys ($1.1 million) with five stocks up, two down and three flat. NFI units rose 0.7 percent to 141 zlotys ($49.1) and rose 1.4 percent to 143 zlotys ($49.8) in live trade.
